title: ACD setup
blurb: The inbound voice path: skill, script, DNIS, and the point of contact that binds them.

lessons.title: The inbound voice order
lessons.summary: Set Up Inbound Voice builds a phone skill, a phone script, and a point of contact, in that order. The DNIS already has to exist.
objectives: Follow the published order
Name the permissions
Leave the DNIS to Professional Services

sections.h: What the page tells you to create
p: Set Up Inbound Voice says to create an inbound phone ACD skill with Media Type Phone Call and direction Inbound, pick a campaign, and name the skill. Permissions are ACD > Skills Create, Edit.

You then create a phone script. The page says to add BEGIN and REQAGENT and connect them. Inbound calls route to the skill on the point of contact unless you change the Skill property on REQAGENT. An IVR, if you want one, is added in the script, and the page says you may need your account representative for guidance.

Create the POC in ACD under Contact Settings > Points of Contact, media type Phone Call. Choose the DNIS from the drop-down of numbers already configured with NiCE. Select the skill and the script. IVR Reporting Enabled is how that number tracks IVR press paths.
The points of contact overview adds the prerequisite the setup page assumes: Professional Services configures the phone number before you can build a POC for it.

lessons.title: Skill name, campaign, and direction
lessons.summary: A skill has a media type, a direction, a name, and a campaign. Priority fields, including acceleration, live on the skill and are not the same thing as proficiency.
objectives: Fill the required skill fields
Keep priority separate from proficiency
Use the documented priority formula later, not here

p: Create New > Single Skill. Media Type Phone Call. Inbound/Outbound set to Inbound. Enter a skill name. Select the campaign. The page says the remaining Skill Information fields are optional.

Priority is one of those later fields. The static delivery page defines Initial Priority, Acceleration, and Maximum Priority. Overall Priority = (Time × Acceleration) + Initial Priority. That math is not the skill's name and not the agent's proficiency.

cites.title: Configure Priority for a Skill for Static Delivery

sections.h: Proficiency is on the agent assignment
p: Bullseye says that when you assign an agent to a skill you also set proficiency, from 1 to 20, where 1 is best and 20 is worst. You can set it on the ACD user profile or on the skill record.
A skill without agents, or agents without a proficiency you intended, will not match the window your script requests. The skill can exist and still deliver to nobody.

steps: Skill A: initial 4, acceleration 1, age 3 minutes. Write 7.

lessons.title: Bind the point of contact
lessons.summary: The point of contact is the only object that joins a specific number to one skill and one script. Reporting for IVR presses is a flag on that object.
objectives: Create a single POC
Select an existing DNIS
Decide on IVR reporting

p: App selector, ACD, Contact Settings, Points of Contact, Create New, Single Point of Contact. Media type Phone Call. Name it. Pick the DNIS. Pick the skill you created. Pick the script. Optionally enable IVR reporting. Create.
Permission on that page: ACD > Contact Settings > Points of Contact Create.

sections.h: Sharing is across POCs, not inside one
p: Several numbers can point at the same script when the menu is the same and the default skill differs, or the reverse. Each row is still one skill and one script.

Email POCs use an email address instead of a DNIS. Digital POCs are created under Digital > Points of Contact and use the digital channel you choose. Do not build a chat channel on the phone POC form.

lessons.title: Hours, closed paths, and what this lab will not invent
lessons.summary: The inbound page says you may add an IVR in the script and that you may need an account representative. It does not, in the passage used here, document an hours action field by field. Closed treatment has to be designed, and unknown actions stay marked unknown.
objectives: Keep undocumented actions out of a design
Plan a closed path as a product question
Use Menu only for what Menu's page says

figure.caption: Open path and a question mark

sections.h: Stay on the pages you have
p: The basic script tutorial builds a menu, requests an agent, and plays hold music until the agent answers. The Menu page says the action plays a prompt and stores the contact's entry in a variable you name.

An hours or holiday branch is a real contact-center need. This lab does not invent the Studio action name, properties, or branch labels for hours of operation. Look up the current action page before you put one in a design, and treat any remembered property list as uncertain.
You can specify the experience you want: a closed prompt, no queue, and a hang-up or a callback offer. You then map that experience onto actions the current help actually documents.

Virtual hold, as the Studio product page describes it, disconnects the caller and creates a callback when an agent is available. That is a product claim on the Studio integration page, not a field list.

lessons.title: The script the POC actually runs
lessons.summary: A beautiful script that is not selected on the point of contact does not run. The POC holds exactly one script name.
objectives: Select the script on the POC
Retarget skills inside the script
Notice a script that is merely saved

p: The inbound setup's last move is selecting the script on the point of contact. Studio Fundamentals says scripts assigned to POCs must define the flow from the start of the interaction on that channel.
Editing a different script, or saving a new version under a new name and forgetting the POC, leaves production on the old flow. The platform is doing what the POC says.

sections.h: Inside the script you may still branch
p: The one script can contain many Reqagent actions. The tutorial tells you to pick, on each branch, an inbound phone skill that matches that menu destination, and to assign that skill to the agents who should answer.
That is how one POC script becomes sales, support, and billing without three points of contact.

lessons.title: Campaigns hold skills
lessons.summary: The skill form requires a campaign. Reporting and later staffing talk about skills. The campaign is the folder you chose at create time.
objectives: Select a campaign when creating a skill
Not confuse campaign with tenant
Not confuse campaign with POC

p: Set Up Inbound Voice tells you to select the campaign the skill should be part of. It does not, in that procedure, ask you to create the campaign. If you have no campaign, that is a separate setup question for your tenant's ACD configuration, not a step this page spells out.
Putting a skill in the wrong campaign does not change the POC rule. The point of contact still points at the skill by name. Reports and WFM that filter by campaign can still look wrong.
The UCCE connector page says historical skill-based data is what Forecasting and Staffing use. Inside CXone, the forecast page also works from skills and historical ACD data.
A campaign is not a WFM scheduling unit unless your WFM configuration says so. This lab does not invent that mapping.

lessons.title: Permissions along the setup path
lessons.summary: The inbound page names skill and POC permissions, and script create permission. A person who can build a script may still be unable to attach it.
objectives: Quote the three permissions the page names
Expect a missing button to be a role
Keep API keys out of this path

p: Skill work: ACD > Skills Create, Edit. Script work, on the setup page: ACD > Contact Settings > Scripts Create. POC work: ACD > Contact Settings > Points of Contact Create.
Those strings are easy to shorten in a ticket until someone cannot click Create. Paste the full string into the access request.
The Admin page is where the role gains those permissions. An implementer with Studio open and no POC permission will finish the script and stop.
This path does not use an access key. Keys are for applications. A human implementer uses a role and a login authenticator.
